trundle.title: Trundle
trundle.description:
Trundle was whelped in a filthy cave, along with a brood of fifteen brothers and sisters. Times were particularly hard, so that only seven of them grew strong enough to join the ranks of their chieftain's warband... and only three remained after their first winter of raiding.

As the warband feasted, the chieftain spoke of his intention to circle back and raid the same lands again. All would fear them. It would get easier every time.

Frowning, Trundle stood up, and said this plan was no good. The people they had crushed had nothing left for the tribe to take—they should return next winter when the granaries were full again, and the livestock grown big enough to make more than a single mouthful.

Many of the other trolls did not like this at all. They ground their teeth and thumped the sides of their heads, trying to comprehend what Trundle was suggesting. Was he a coward? Had the cold got into his brain and turned it to slush? The chieftain beat Trundle with a rock, and threw him away down the mountainside. Fools had no place in his warband.

Trundle wandered far, for he knew he would not be welcome anywhere nearby. He avoided other troll tribes scattered across the tundra, and was careful to keep his distance from the feral yetis that roamed the highlands. By night, he gazed up at the stars and remembered all the stories he had been told as a pup—legends of Grubgrack the Wise, and other ancient troll kings, who followed the old gods and were gifted powerful weapons as symbols of their right to rule the world.

Eventually, Trundle came to a great crack in the ground. While he was glad to be out of the wind, he soon found himself lost in a maze of twisted, howling canyons that seemed to sink deeper beneath the Freljord than the mountains rose above it.

kobolds.title: Kobolds of the Emberdeep
kobolds.subheader: Trap-savvy clutch networks within the Emberdeep caldera
kobolds.description:
![Kobolds gathering in a lava-lit cavern with banners](images/3ed13064f54fa486a48442c62c8bfb57.jpg)

## Overview

Kobolds are a bipedal race of subterranean dragonkin that typically range in size from that of a Gnome to a Dwarf. For ages these reptilian attackes had been one of the Great Scourges of Dwarfkind, though just like their larger Dargonine relative, their numerous nature has declined in recent years and they've become more uncommon, leading them to be downgraded to simply a threat rather than a Great Threat.

## Burrow Structure

Spiral warrens align living quarters with radiant heat while ventilation shafts serve as message tubes for pebble-code rattles. Key districts include:

- **Surface Apertures** — camouflaged skylights feeding lichen gardens and providing emergency egress during lava surges.
- **Ember Galleries** — communal smelters that cycle cinders through rotating cages to prevent flare-ups.
- **Dragon Vaults** — mirrorstone-lined tithe chambers with counterweighted floors ready to seal if diplomacy fails.

## Trapcraft and Engineering

Defense doctrine favors misdirection via dummy tunnels, thunder-pot echo chambers, and rolling cages that corral intruders toward negotiation platforms. Cavern Census advisories warn against tampering with lichen lanterns that hide flame siphons and recommend resonant chimes to disrupt pebble-code transmissions.

## Tribute and Trade

Tithes manifest as gemstone chimes tuned to a patron drake's favored frequencies, paired with automata that sweep volcanic ash from dragon scales. Surface commerce trades fireglass lenses, collapsible lantern poles, magma vein maps, and wartime sapper expertise for allied sieges.

## Myth and Oathbinding

Burrow Choir chants recount the First Ember coaxing a star-egg into the caldera. Oaths seal when kobolds press claws to heated anvilstones while reciting lineage spirals, and the decennial Sapphire Accord renewal warns that faltering the rhythm awakens the Ashwind sentinel to dissolve treacherous cooperatives.

## Field Notes

1. Archivist Tolan Nerys, *Emberdeep Census Rolls* (Cavern Archives, Case 12).
2. Ironbridge collapse rescue accounts transcribed by Burrow Choir scribes.
3. Drakespine tributary receipts from the Sapphire Accord editions 1885–1894.

northmen.title: Northmen Raiders
northmen.subheader: Feared seaborne raiders from the northern fjords
northmen.description:
## Overview

The Northmen are a maritime people of the high fjords, renowned for swift longships, fearless axe crews, and coastal strikes that arrive with the first fog. Their settlements cling to wind-scoured cliffs where shipwright clans and oathbound jarls rule by right of raid, trade, and sea-law.

## Culture and Society

Northmen life is defined by **oath rings**, communal hearths, and a strict code of hospitality that balances raiding with honor. Jarls convene at seasonal **thingmoots**, where disputes are settled by sworn testimony and gifts of iron or amber. Skalds memorize lineage sagas and recite them before voyages to bind crews with shared purpose.

## Seafaring and Raiding

Longships are built with overlapping pine planks sealed in tar and whale oil, allowing them to beach quickly and retreat just as fast. Raiding bands prefer dawn tides, using smoke beacons and horn calls to coordinate across coves. While feared for sudden assaults, Northmen also levy tolls on trade routes and offer escort services through storm-choked passes.

## Arms and Craft

Northmen weapons favor practicality: broad axes for shipboard fighting, short spears for boarding, and round shields painted with clan sigils. Smiths craft **storm-tempered steel** by quenching blades in brine mixed with volcanic ash, claiming it sharpens both edge and spirit.

## Relations and Reputation

Coastal towns fortify harbors and pay tribute to avoid raids, yet many merchants willingly trade with Northmen for furs, whale ivory, and stormglass charms. Their reputation as ruthless raiders is tempered by strict ransoming customs and a tradition of honoring oaths once terms are struck.

## Field Notes

1. Captain Rysa Holt, *Logs of the Greywake*, entries 12–29 describing Northmen longship tactics.
2. Archivist Halden Skar, "Songs of the Fjord" — skaldic verses compiled at the Skysteel Hall.
3. Harbor Watch records, Frostfjord Treaty of 1812, detailing tribute and escort agreements.

ogre.title: Gravelmaw Ogres
ogre.subheader: Siege savants commanding mobile quarry camps
ogre.description:
![Ogre engineers raising a stone bulwark](images/9f0b1c3b4a679a38796831d7a79647c1.jpg)

## Overview

Gravelmaw ogres roam canyon networks hauling collapsible siege foundries atop chain-dragged sledges. Their culture centers on quarrying resonant stone used to reinforce frontier bastions or, when negotiations fail, to shatter enemy keeps.

## Clan Organization

Clans revolve around **Spanmasters** who chart stress fractures across canyon bridges. Forge-priests maintain rhythm anvils tuned to canyon winds, ensuring every hammer strike aligns with structural weak points. Young ogres apprentice as haulrunners before earning the right to wield the clan's seismic mauls.

## Warfare and Engineering

Their weapons include ripple rams that emit focused shockwaves, collapsible rampart kits, and obsidian-tipped chain bolas capable of toppling siege towers. Defensive tactics feature layered boulder curtains rigged to drop sequentially while drummers coordinate countercharges.

## Trade and Diplomacy

Gravelmaw diplomats broker stone reinforcement services, demanding in return ironwood struts, alchemical lubricants, and rights to salvage battle debris. Honor feasts feature basalt-baked root stews, and treaties are etched onto balanced counterweights hung in neutral ravines.

## Field Notes

1. Engineer Myra Feldt's battlefield sketches of ripple ram deployments during the Siege of Breakwater Arch.
2. Granite Ledger entries documenting trade agreements with the River Watch.
3. Oral recital of Drum-Captain Rulgar describing the Pact of Three Echoes.

orc.title: Orcish Strongholds
orc.subheader: Border Marches martial societies and seasonal keeps
orc.description:
![Terraced orcish stronghold lit by volcanic embers](images/markus-neidel-woa-poi-illustration-orc-stronghold-1920.jpg)

## Overview

Orcish polities of the Border Marches descend from thunder-crow migrations and balance martial readiness with a ritual calendar that governs hunting, ironworking, and diplomacy. Blood-keeps pledge stone-singers, stewards, and warriors to a rotating high warband, while relay shrines offer safe passage to travelers who present water at their altars.

## Clan Societies

Confederacy envoys describe consensus councils held beneath the Black Pines where drum-bearing delegates can postpone war plans for a lunar cycle. Three principal circles anchor these gatherings:

- **Storm Banner Circle** — frontier guardians who field ashlance cavalry and maintain avalanche beacons.
- **Ember Hearth Circle** — metallurgists and surgeons who trade surgical knotwork for dyes and glassware.
- **Verdant Tide Circle** — riverine logisticians who manage barge libraries and seed exchanges.

## Stronghold Architecture

Surveyors note concentric terraces carved from basalt with communal forges on lower rings and dream interpreter quarters atop. Alternating crenellations and horn totems hide thunderstones tuned to clan rhythms, creating humming ramparts during storms. Captain Yara Estwin credits stone-singer resonance for the keeps' resistance to artillery.

## Material and Ritual Culture

Every warrior maintains a practical field blade and a ceremonial twin etched with storms they have outrun; a blade is retired only when the lineage raises a new stone-singer. Seasonal rites pair martial drills with hospitality, serving fermented pine sap to allies before the polyphonic **Song of Ashes** recounts founding migrations.

## Alliances and Treaties

Confederate councils weave a braided **cord of witness** that records accords renewed each year. Key strands include the **Stonewake Compact (1742)** with Karthi River monasteries, the **Second Ember Exchange (1821)** trading copper for aurora dyes, and the **Stormgate Concord (1968)** pledging mutual defense against airship fleets. Severing a strand demands the offender broker three new treaties or accept exile.

## Field Notes

1. Captain Yara Estwin, "Observations from the Stormcrag Frontier" — engineering notebook folios 14–29 describing thunderstone maintenance.
2. Emissary Hallan of the Verdant Tide — recorded interview archived at the Black Pines lodge covering barge libraries and oath circles.
3. Caravan Master Edeya Lor, *Ledger of the Sapphire Route*, entries 223–264 on trade etiquette at dawn markets.
4. Wax cylinder of the Storm Banner Circle chant captured by Professor I. Farsen (1903), corroborating the layers of the Song of Ashes.

piracy.title: Pirate Freeports
piracy.subheader: Maritime syndicates and oathbound corsair havens
piracy.description:
![Pirate fleet anchored in a lantern-lit cove](images/pirate-cove-fleet.jpg)

## Overview

Pirate freeports rise where tidal coves meet hidden sea tunnels, governed by compact councils of captains, quartermasters, and dockwardens. They regulate salvage rights, divide spoils through sealed ledgers, and provide sanctuary to crews who honor the Saltwind charter.

## Governance and Codes

The Saltwind confederacy convenes each equinox beneath the black-beacon lighthouse. Decisions require a three-helm vote, balancing captains, navigators, and stevedores. Oathmarks inked on wrists record allegiances and are renewed annually during the Tidefire ceremony.

## Trade and Logistics

Freeports thrive on clandestine commerce: reef pilots guide contraband through shoals, while cooperative chandlers outfit ships with stormglass compasses and alchemical pitch. A standardized tally system prevents feuds by auditing cargo swaps in public taverns.

## Fleet Doctrine

Corsair wings favor fast skimmers with collapsible masts, striking in synchronized sweeps that disable sails before boarding. Veteran crews train with signal drums and mirrored pennants, allowing coordinated attacks across fog banks and moonlit bays.

## Field Notes

1. First Mate Rilla Sunwaft, *Ledger of the Saltwind Freeports* (Harbor Registry 201).
2. Admiral Crestin Hale, "On Corsair Compacts" — personal letters archived in the Tideglass Vault.
3. Survey of the Black-Beacon Lighthouse foundations, annotated by Engineer Kiyo Marr.

ratling.title: Underrail Ratlings
ratling.altNames: Pipeway couriers of the Buried Market
ratling.subheader: Scavenger cooperatives orchestrating hidden trade spines
ratling.description:
![Ratling brokers negotiating in lantern-lit tunnels](images/8b1c45d43af25e58471fd9b2ec687e38.jpg)

## Overview

Ratlings maintain labyrinthine pipeways beneath industrial quarters, mapping every maintenance shaft and forgotten cistern. Their whiskered scouts memorize vibration signatures to detect intruders long before they enter the warrens.

## Collective Structure

Cooperatives known as **Clatterbands** pool resources and vote via tail-knot codes tied to communal signal lines. Quartermasters record obligations on chew-resistant slate tablets coated in resin, ensuring ledgers survive steam bursts and chemical runoff.

## Tradecraft and Intelligence

Ratlings broker salvage rights, smuggle contraband botanicals, and run messenger relays through humming pneumatic tubes. Field agents wield wrist-mounted hooklaunchers to cross chasms, and archivists train scent-tracking ferrets to guard repository vaults.

## Relations with Surface Dwellers

Surface guilds respect ratling neutrality by depositing tribute caches at designated drain grates. Offenders who shortchange a tribute awaken to their warehouses rearranged overnight, inventory carefully accounted for with annotations explaining corrective interest.

## Field Notes

1. Buried Market manifest BM-19 cataloguing tribute exchanges during the Copper Moon.
2. Inspector Harrow's testimony on ratling intervention in halting a plague-bearing barge.
3. Tail-knot cipher primer distributed to allied couriers after the Steam-Tunnel Truce.

red-curse.title: The Red Curse
red-curse.altNames: Saffron Blight of the Blood March
red-curse.subheader: Crimson affliction that stains stone and spirit alike
red-curse.description:
## Overview

The Red Curse is a slow-moving malady that first blooms as a faint rust streak in mortar, then spreads into living flesh as fevered crimson veining. Chroniclers note its arrival after the third Ember Exchange, when smelters ran night and day and the ash-sky never cleared.

## Signs and Progression

Early symptoms include metallic taste, sleep-heavy limbs, and a red dust that clings to tools and skin. In later stages the afflicted hear distant forge bells, while masonry around them develops hairline fractures that widen with every oath broken nearby.

## Cultural Response

Border guilds treat the curse as a civic emergency; quarantines are sealed with sootglass wards and posted with red-ink ledgers. Dwarven enclaves interpret the curse as a warning against unbalanced extraction and host emberfast vigils to restore the deepforge cadence.

## Containment Practices

Most remedies focus on balance: closing mine vents, dampening furnaces, and marking afflicted stones with cooling glyphs to redirect the curse. A shared ritual called the **Quiet Pour** requires saltwater libations poured into abandoned seams while apprentices recite the names of the lost.

## Field Notes

1. Archivist Merel Thorne, *Chronicle of the Saffron Blight* (River Guild Annex, folio 18).
2. Healer Nessa Drel, treatment logs from the Emberfast Ward, entries 201–237.
3. The Ashline Council proclamation sealing the fourth forgeway during the Red Moon.

religion.title: Religion of the Holds
religion.altNames: The Forgefaith and the River Canticles
religion.subheader: Shared rites that bind clans, guilds, and wandering circles
religion.description:
## Overview

Religion in the Holds blends forge-rituals, river hymns, and seasonal observances into a living calendar. While each clan keeps its own patron spirits, most rites honor the balance between craft, kinship, and the land that sustains their halls.

## The Forgefaith

The Forgefaith centers on reverence for the **Anvil of First Heat**, an origin myth that teaches endurance through tempered labor. Devotees mark milestones by quenching newly forged tools in shared basins, symbolizing communal stewardship of work and wealth.

## River Canticles

River cantors guide processions that bless barges and trade routes with antiphonal chants. These hymns are believed to align tides with safe passage and are taught to apprentices alongside ledgerkeeping to reinforce honest exchange.

## Household Observances

Home altars often feature three stones: one for ancestors, one for the living hearth, and one left uncarved for the unknown. Offerings range from grain and coal to small crafted tokens left for travelers in need.

## Interclan Concords

Shared festivals, such as the **Emberfast Vigil** and the **First Thaw Procession**, bring disparate clans together. Oathkeepers oversee these gatherings to ensure disputes are paused and old agreements are honored before trade resumes.

## Field Notes

1. Cantor Lyra Fen, *Rites of the River Guild* (Ledger Hall Press, 1902).
2. Hearthwarden Thane Brill, notes on Emberfast Vigils kept in the Stonefast archives.
3. Festival rolls from the First Thaw Procession, Sunmeadow Barrows registry.

troglodyte.title: Troglodytes
troglodyte.altNames: Myconic wardens of the Fumarole Veins
troglodyte.subheader: Bioluminary guardians thriving in caustic depths
troglodyte.description:
![Troglodytes tending glowing fungus pools](images/5f5b18f639c3de5407fdbbf9784d5a53.jpg)

## Overview

Troglodyte communes inhabit volcanic fault lines where mineral fog shrouds obsidian terraces. Their translucent skin refracts the neon glow of alchemical fungi cultivated in tiered pools.

## Physiology and Culture

Residents undergo **Fume Baptisms** that acclimate lungs to sulfur-saturated air, allowing them to breathe unfiltered within vents that would choke surface folk. Communal memory is preserved through scent-coded chants—each aroma triggers specific verses carried on harmonic clicks.

## Defense and Rituals

Guardian cadres wield crystallized acid shards and deploy pheromone mists that disorient trespassers. Festivals commemorate eruptions with synchronized bioluminescent dances, painting the cavern ceiling with patterns interpreted by seers as omens of tectonic calm or upheaval.

## External Relations

Troglodytes trade stabilizing salves, glowstone capacitors, and steam-shield plating to subterranean allies. In exchange they request breathable moss spores, metal ingots resistant to corrosion, and stories recorded on scent-infused scrolls.

## Field Notes

1. Mineralogical survey SM-88 verifying acid shard growth cycles.
2. Diplomacy log of Envoy Cassia Wyrmguard documenting steam-shield barter terms.
3. Scent-scroll fragments translated by Scholar Ojun Rel, revealing the prophecy of the Twin Eruptions.

tram.title: Tram
tram.description:
![Dwarf Tram](images/Dwarf%20Tram.jpg)


A tram  is a form of steam-powered rail transport consisting of a series of connected carriages placed behind a locomotive outfitted with a steam engine burning wood or coal that generally run along a railroad or railway track to transport passengers or cargo. In the Known World. Trams are a recent invention of the Dwavern Engineering guild.

## Construction
Dwavern engineering teams favor low-slung boiler frames to keep the carriage chain stable on narrow passes. Standard carriages include removable bench slats for passenger service and reinforced hook points for cargo lashings.

## Operations
Guild dispatchers schedule tram movements by whistle code, timing departures to avoid shared track conflicts with ore haulers. Conductors keep logbooks that record coal consumption, carriage counts, and any repairs required at the next depot.

yeti.title: Yetis
yeti.description:
![Yeti oracle tracing glyphs in blowing snow](images/Events/Yeti.jpg)

## Overview

Shardspine yetis roam knife-edged ridges where aurora curtains scrape the peaks. Clans follow migrating starfalls, sheathing their white fur in crushed sapphire dust to refract hostile light. Surface caravans track their movements by the echo of bone flutes drifting through blizzards.

## Habitat and Society

Trance-lodges are carved within blue-ice chambers that hum with glacial resonance. Elders called **Frost-Readers** suspend crystal pendulums that record tectonic murmurs, while the **Avalanche Chorus** shapes snowpack with low-frequency throat songs. No single leader rules; decisions thaw only after each circle contributes a verse to the omen tally.

## Survival Practices

Yetis weave heat-trapping cloaks from snowmoss and glacier goat wool, sealing them with whale oil traded from fjord raiders. Their diet combines fermented lichen bricks, frozen marrow shards, and stormbird eggs cached in geothermal vents. When storms rage, they braid warning totems into crevasses so wanderers can tether themselves to safety lines.

## Diplomacy and Lore

Frostbound emissaries exchange aurora charts for star-metal chisels, insisting on moot circles held at twilight when reflections do not blind them. Storykeepers inscribe visions on obsidian plates kept in pressure-sealed reliquaries; each plate is broken only when corroborating dreams arise among allied shamans.

## Field Notes

1. Polar Survey Expedition Log 43-B describing pendulum omens before the 1874 icequake.
2. Whispered translations of the Avalanche Chorus by linguist Eira Stonethaw, archived in the Boreal Library.
3. Trade scrip ledger noting oil-for-aurora chart exchanges at Frostwind Crag during the most recent thaw conclave.

great-destruction.title: The Great Destruction
great-destruction.description:
The Great Destruction is a name given to the massive Northman led invasion of the civilized world that lead to the total destruction of Rusland, along with the conquering of much of the Empire of Bohemia before the Northman forces were eventually overcome and routed. 


# # Background

For millennia the great Tzardom of Rusland served as a bulwark of humanity, taking the brunt impact of countless invasions and pushing back the enemy forces before they could reach Bohemia. This changed in 2897 when a massive incursion led by the combined might of the Northmen tribes of the Frostmourn mountaints managed to overcome the resistance and crush the Tsars forces.

expatriate-dwarf.title: Expatriate Dwarf
expatriate-dwarf.description:
An Expatriate Dwarf, disparagingly called "Manling Dwarfs" (Umgdawi) or "Flatlanders" (Gazani) by their kinsmen, is a Dwarf who has left the native homelands of their people in the mountains behind to seek a new life in the lands of Men.

With the decline of the Dwarf people and the fall of many holds, mines, and settlements, a number of Dwarf clans descended into the forested flatlands from the mountains. Some settled in Human lands, drawn by the high prices their work can demand among the Manlings. Others chose exile following a dispute with their clansmen or their lord, or because of some grudge. To the Dwarfs, these rootless Dwarfs (Ruebatuki or "Ruebs" for short) have turned their backs on both kin and tradition.

war-of-the-boar.title: The War of the Boar
war-of-the-boar.subheader: Conflict between the Boers and the Orcish Horde during the Orcish Invasion of Azeroth
war-of-the-boar.description:
The War of the Boar was the name for the conflicts between the Boers and the Orcish Horde during the Orcish Invasion of Azeroth. The War of the Boar was known to have been a pyrrhic victory for the Boers, as despite beating the Orcs and pushing them out of the mountainous hillsides in the east, many communities were lost in the Rooiwatersrand and the Goudland, as a result of scorched earth tactics.

## Contents
1. The Vaal-land Campaign
2. The Goudland Campaign
3. The Natalia Campaign
4. Memory and Legacy

## The Vaal-land Campaign
The war began when Orcish forces encountered Boer forces in the southernmost region of Zundrboek- the Vaal-land, located north of the Vaal River. The Orcs were led by a warlord by the name of Kargor Bloodsong, chieftain of the Bloodsong Tribe, a subsect of the larger Dragonmaw Clan. The first battle of the war involved the taking of the settlement of Vaalhavn- Harbor on the Vaal. Vaalhavn was a major center of trade towards the communities of Eastern Arathor, and thus the taking of the community was a large problem for commercial trade. The capturing of Vaalhavn prompted Krugar Boergraf to take immediate action, which included sending forth the Andries Fusilers Korps into the territory of the Vaal-land. The Andries Fusiliers Corps, numbering a total of two hundred members, marched into the Vaal-land two days after the taking of Vaalhavn. Upon arrival, the Fusiliers cooperated with siege engineers on preparing the large town of Vaalstad for a defensive attack. A mandatory retreat was ordered of all persons in the Vaal-land to the city of Vaalstad. Kargor's men feasted on what they had captured in the wealthy city of Vaalhavn for two days, allowing the evacuation to commence. After the two day evacuation had taken place, nearly five hundred citizens had been recalled to Vaalstad.

The field marshall of the Andries Fusilier Corps- Klaas Willem van Ruiter, gave an order in the Vaalstad to arm all able bodied men and women for battle against the Orcs, who were now advancing. Krugar called for an immediate arming of the militias in the other portions of Zundrboek, and for a securing of all necessary resources. Several smaller towns were forced to retreat back to larger towns by law. Among many of the cities that were deemed "necessary" for the war effort were Vaalstad, Kaapstad, Klipfontein, Boerstad, Andriestor, and Boerdijk.

Klaas Willem van Ruiter met the army of Kargor along the large sea walls on the Vaal River. Orcish forces sailed northwards on smaller canoe-like ships. The Fusiliers operated fifteen small artillery pieces, which were implemented at this stage of the initial landing. In addition to having forty five men operating the fifteen artillery pieces, an additional fifty five marksmen were deployed in the region, from among the local population. Van Ruiter's plan was to create a situation in which the Orcs would take in so much damage they would be unable to advance, aiming towards overkill. The fields surrounding Vaalstad were filled with mines, which had been planted by the engineers of the Fusilier Corps, who handled them with care. In the fields, two hundred and fifty mines had been planted.

Kargor had deployed five hundred of his three thousand Orcs towards the taking of the Vaal-land. These five hundred Orcs were going up against the Fusiliers' one hundred and an additional seven hundred civilian drafters. Kargor's forces were led by his lieutenant- Lamnogg Goreslayer. Lamnogg's experience had included the slaughtering of several dwarven towns in the Wetlands during the Khaz Modan campaign. Lamnogg had a reputation as a fierce and brutal commander, and often his rage would cloud his mind. On the front lines, van Ruiter's artillery commander- Andrij van Sterkgeweer, led the first line of defense. Andrij's forces held out for eighteen hours straight of fighting. The artillerymen and riflemen had sustained next to no casualties, however Lamnogg's forces had lost nearly seventy five Orcs. Many of the Orcs went by sea, but held themselves in small caves that had been hidden by the elements, or simply took cover on the beachhead.

Andrij's forces retreated back towards the second line of defense, which was a second part of the strategy, developed by Van Ruiter's second-in-command, Rolan van Boergeweer. Rolan's plan was to create a series of trenches one thousand yards behind Van Sterkgeweer's artillery posts were on the beachhead. The trenches were easily dug by the large amount of civlian volunteers, and were well stocked with food, water, and ammunition.

Andrij forces wheeled back the artillery, and it was only nearly an hour after their retreat that Lamnogg was able to find out that the Dwarves had in fact retreated. Andrij's forces supplanted the one hundred fighters at the trenches, who were apart of the Slootkorps, or Trench Corps. The Slootkorps were well disciplined soldiers in the Fusiliers Regiment, and were led by Helmut van Sloot. The trench lines were designed to hold back the Orcs for as long as possible, which they were successful in doing.

Several trench lines had been left open to confuse the Orcs, and were lined with more primal landmines, in contrast to the advanced land mines that had been used on the beach-head. These lines were known as the Vaalslooten, and were able to hold back the Orcs for two days. Lamnogg's initial charge involved the taking of one trench. In conquering the first trench, which was full of mines, his forces lost fifty men. Lamnogg established the first trench as his center of command to launch attacks, and a Goblin was sent back with news announcing the control of the beachhead and a trench, albeit a need of additional manpower.

Kargor's response to this was to send in an additional one hundred soldiers, led by his younger cousin- Garokk Bloodsong. Garokk's addiitional forces allowed for Lamnogg to order a full charge, which was a very foolish move. The Slootkorps had trapped three trenches in front of them, which claimed many lives. However, when the Orcs came into view, the Slootkorps were able to slaughter nearly one hundred additional soldiers, tallying up the orc losses to two hundred and twenty five. The majority of the Slootkorps perished in the trenches, including Helmut, as well as Andrij's remaining soldiers. Ammunition was carried back to Vaalstad, along with food and water, while the trenches were filled with gasoline which was promptly burned. The burning of the trenches stalled Lamnogg's advance towards Vaalstad for twenty hours, until the fire burned itself out. Lamnogg's capturing of the trenches is often regarded as a large military defeat for the Andries Fusiliers, who were known to have never lost a battle.

The third line of defense was located inside the city, and was the entire city. At this point, ammunition was distributed, alongside the remaining military ordinance inside the town's armory and what was left from the trenches. Citizens were commanded to do what they could and band together, but do their best to kill as many Orcs as they could inside their homes in swift attacks. The Fusiliers were distributed throughout Vaalstad in the homes to ensure that citizens were able to defend themselves. The sick, elderly, and children were all sent down into the mines of Vaalstad, where there was food and water stored.

Lamnogg wrote to Kargor asking for more soldiers after his assault on the trenches, but Kargor refused and told him to assault the gates with what he had, believing the will to fight was broken.

Krugar Boergraf wrote to Van Ruiter, telling him that he would be executed if his forces returned back to Kaapstad without a victory on their backs. Krugar's warning encouraged morale, although at a price. Van Ruiter implemented a "No Man Steps Backwards" rule, which meant that deserters would be thrown to the Orcs.

The Orcs broke through Vaalstad's Wall after five hours of assault, and entered the city. This proved to be a fatal mistake, as within the first hour, there were numerous civilian ambushes. Lamnogg's original plan had been to simply march to the top and slay the leader of the Vaal-landers and the Andries Fusiliers, hoping that morale would drop and the Dwarves would give up the will to fight. He was forced to divide his remaining two hundred and seventy forces into five man squads to clear the village house by house, which proved to be extremely ineffective. Some houses were rigged with traps that brought down their foundations, others were full of Dwarves with firearms, others were simply wastes of time.

Krugar Boergraf meanwhile, had successfully fortified the three essential provinces of Natalia-land, also known as Vrijstad, or "Free City," Rijkland, which contained the City of Kaapstad, and the province of Goudland, which was known for its production of Gold among other metals. The region of the Kaap (divided into three provinces- Noordkaap, Zuidkaap, and Oostkaap) was also held, although not significantly because it lacked a direct area to be attacked by the Orcs, as the Orcs did not sail in the area of the Thandol Span.

The Battle of Vaal-stad continued on for ten more days, until Lamnogg was killed by Van Ruiter in the city square. The Orcs had successfully taken down nearly one hundred houses and killed well over two hundred Vaal-landers, however the death of Lamnogg caused a total collapse in the army. Garokk was slain by Rolan six hours before the Assault on the City Square, which had been a prime motivator of Lamnogg's anger. The death of Lamnogg and failure of the Vaal-land campaign caused Kargor to go into a rage of bloodlust, and in his anger, he deployed all soldiers at the expense into Zundrboek under his own leadership. Furthermore, Kargor killed his three commanding officers of the army, including his son, his uncle (father of Garokk), and the older brother of Lamnogg.

After the victory at the battle of Vaal-stad, Krugar Boergraf sent forward one hundred additional soldiers from the Arnon Bergklimmer Regiment. The Bergklimmers were led by Carolus van Kalkhoven. Carolus linked up with the remnants of the Andries Fusiliers, along with the Vaal-lander Militia. The two began plans for an assault to retake the city of Vaalhavn, which was interrupted after the Bloodsong Orcs marched northwards and attacked Goudland, one of the heavily fortified provinces. Kargor had two thousand five hundred troops at his disposal, while Krugar had merely one thousand soldiers and an additional five hundred registered militia. This sudden movement meant that Carolus and Van Ruiter could wrap around the forces advancing northwards from their position in the south. This is what their main plan became. Vaalhavn was established as a center of Orcish supplies, and was staffed by fifty Orcs from a fellow clan- the Deadcleavers, which were focused on attacking the main area of the Arathi Highlands. The Fifty Deadcleaver Orcs were known for their strength, and so it was that the group would have problems in retaking the city on their own.

Van Ruiter ordered that the artillery pieces, which had been wheeled back into the trenches and then into the City Square, were to be wheeled out with fresh ammunition, which was another supply that the Bergklimmer Regiment had brought with them. Van Ruiter's plan was to assault Vaalhavn, which was a lowland area, using the cannons, and then sending in his warriors to clean up whatever remained.

Van Ruiter commenced his attack after three days of marching and planning. Van Ruiter's artillery shelled Vaalhavn for sixteen hours straight, utilizing the fifteen cannons. The Deadcleavers didn't stand a chance, as they lacked strong ranged combat, as their name suggests. The Deadcleavers were mainly suited towards close quarters combat, and based off of the fight that the Dwarves of Khaz Modan had put up, the Deadcleavers and Bloodsongs assumed combat to be the same against the Boers. The Deadcleavers had been killed, with a few stray Goblin thralls taking cover in basements. The retaking of Vaalhavn severely disrupted the supply line.

Van Ruiter spent an additional week gathering forces in the south, including the forces of the Riebeck Fusiliers Korps and the Wulfart Jagerkorps. In total, Van Ruiter had gathered an additional seven hundred men with which to march northwards to reinforce Krugar Boergraf's northern provincial defense force. This ended the Vaal-land Campaign.

## The Goudland Campaign
The Goudland and Natalia Campaign began when the Bloodsongs moved northwards following the holding of Vaalhavn by the Deadcleavers. The Bloodsongs advanced northwards towards Goudland along the Goudweg. The first battle of the Goudland Campaign was the Battle of Goudwater. Goudwater was a major mining community in the Goudland, and was one of the designated "hold out areas" in the province of Goudland. Goudwater had a supply line that went from the fertile soil of the Kaapland, through Rijkland, up to the fertile soil of Natalia/Vrijstad, and then into Goudstad. The battle of Goudwater occurred when the Bloodsong Offensive hit an inhabited community.

The Bloodsongs did have a disadvantage however. Before marching, Kargor had limited the amount of supplies they could take, believing that word of the assault had not yet reached the other parts of the County of Zundrboek. Kargor believed that he would be able to hunt down numerous communities on the way northwards and secure food and other supplies for his soldiers. This turned out to be false, and his men were largely worn down by the time they reached Goudwater. Goudwater was garrisoned with two hundred and fifty soldiers, which were unable to make an effective resistance against the Bloodsong Offensive that was ten times their size. The leader of the garrison at Goudwater- Ernst van Boerstoel, gathered his forces and retreated after his scouts reported the large number of Orcs advancing. Ernst attempted to take as much supplies as he could northwards, predominantly food, water, and gold, although he could not take it all. When the Bloodsongs came across another abandoned community, they were considering razing the settlement to the ground until they realized that there was food and water left behind. The Bloodsongs feasted for several days, which allowed word to spread of the large army heading northwards.

In response to rumors that the Bloodsong army had grown nearly four times larger, Krugar Boergraf issued a release ordering that all communites in the Goudland to retreat to the capital city of Goudstad. In addition, Krugar ordered that the soldiers of the Kaapland and Rijkland come together and form a defensive line in the Goudland. Goudwater was a twenty day march from Goudstad, and with the several days of feasting, the soldiers had time. The city of Goudstad was fortified by soldiers from the Goudrand and Houweel, two other major communities that had been designated as holdouts. A large fortress was erected along the Goudweg in the Province of Natalia Vrijstad, which came to be known as Andriestor. Andriestor was a huge fortress about the size of Goudstad, that would serve as a major defense point along the road. Krugar ordered all able-bodied men to be deployed into the war effort. The Royal Armory (Rijk-Arsenaal) was opened up for the public to take weapons from.

The Bloodsongs continued their advance and attacked the city of Goudstad nearly two weeks after stopping in Goudwater. A week's walk back was Andriestor, which had been hastily built, although it was a sturdy area. Krugar Boergraf deployed himself to the front lines and made Andriestor his command center. He had heard about the defeat suffered by the Bloodsongs and asked frequently on the whereabouts of Van Ruiter. Sure enough, word came of Van Ruiter advancing northwards with an army of southerners when the Bloodsong Offensive reached Goudstad. Goudstad's garrison summed up to two thousand soldiers.

The Battle of Goudstad was one of the bloodiest battles, if not the bloodiest battle of the war. The garrison of two thousand made it larger than any other settlement in the County at the time. In addition, the entirety of the Bloodsong Offensive was coming forward towards the garrison. This meant that the two sides were at the highest numbers, and at the time, Goudstad was the most fortified city in Zundrboek. Goudstad's fortifications were so heavy because of the ongoing rush for gold and other precious metals in the Goudland. The Goudland's rich resources proved to be a drawing factor for many to come to its defense.

The Battle of Goudstad began when the Bloodsong Offensive came within the area known as the "Wulfftens Line," named after the son of Ernst van Boerstoel- Wulfften van Boerstoel. The Wulfftens Line began a series of trenches that ran for two miles around the city of Goudstad. The trenches were manned by one thousand five hundred soldiers. The major tactical aspect of the trenches was that they were not connected to one another. The trenches were around ten yards apart from one another, and the terrain steadily grew higher as one progressed upwards. This meant that the trenches were within firing range of one another, and that the Orcs would take heavy casualties advancing up the mountain, as they could not head underground from one trench to another. There were 352 trenches in total, each one yard in length, which fit well for the Dwarven size, however not very well for the much larger Orcs.

In the north, there was a large amount of industry, specifically in Engineering, that had existed since the reign of the Sootbeards in the Colonial Era of +1501 to +1800. In the north, there were three notable munitions factories, which essentially worked on the processing of the thorium in the mountainous region into bullets. This large stock of bullets was tapped into during this battle, during which each trench was given two thousand bullets to work with. Each of the 352 trenches was manned by 4 or 5 soldiers, which meant that the trenches were extremely well stocked. In total, over the past three hundred years, a total of two million bullets had been produced. There were several munitions factories in the south as well, five in total, which had been producing bullets over the past one hundred years, and created a total of 425,531 bullets. In addition to being the bloodiest battle of the war, the Battle of Goudstad was also one of the most costly in terms of ammunition, as well as the longest battle of the war.

The trench lines had to be taken by force Kargor realized, and his strategy of trench hopping could not work here. When his men tried to take over one trench, the forces in the other trench, in addition to the forces inside the current trench would keep them preocupied. Goudstad was by far one of the most fortified settlements in the Arathi Highlands at the time.

On the first day of the attack, Kargor ordered forth a squad of fifty soldiers to begin advancing into the trenches. His Goblin sapper squads had reported that each trench had 4 or 5 soldiers in it, although they had just gone off of three trenches, and had not realized how close they were to one another. This was because the arms were stored inside a small closet that each trench had. The Goblin Sappers had also failed to note the increasing height of each trench. The army of 50 was to be led by Kargor's second lieutenant- Rekras Bloodslayer. The main problem was not in the taking of the first set of five trenches, the problem was about how tired the soldiers got once they reached the next set of trenches. The Boer defenders in the trenches put up a greater fight than the Orcs had ever seen them fight in. Close range weaponry and long range weaponry were both implemented in the first parts of the battle. Orcish soldiers had trouble reaching down into the narrow trenches with their weaponry, and they also had problems swinging their large blades in the trenches. The Boers on the other hand, made use of rifles with bayonets, which were extremely effective. The bayonets proved to be useful in stabbing manuevers, rather than in swinging, whereas the large Orcish axes failed in combat, often hitting or even getting stuck in the side of the trenches. Rekras was able to fully take three trenches before his soldiers were forced to remain in two of the starting trenches, as they were pinned down by fire from the further trenches. The Boer soldiers in the trenches also went on "shifts," and were easily woken at several times during the day. This meant that at no matter what time the Orcs chose to continue advancing upwards, there would still be awake and aware Boers to keep guard.

After several days of not hearing word, Kargor made probably one of the most foolish tactical advances in the War of the Boar and one of the worst in the entire Second War. His forces advanced towards the stronghold of Goudstad with all of their numbers. The small amount of distance and advanced Boer weaponry meant that the Orcs could be fired up on by soldiers from five trenches back. Furthermore, getting the additional two thousand four hundred and fifty soldiers into cover was extremely hard. The Orcs had crowded the two trenches while Rekras had claimed them, and some had been forced to lie on the ground in the slope where it was harder for snipers to target them. Kargor gave the order to Rekras to charge the trenches, foolishly underestimating the amount of munitions that each trench had. Kargor went through heavy fighting and eventually was able to claim ten more trenches until his soldiers were worn out from fatigue in battle, and he had lost over one hundred men in the assault, including all of his lieutenants- Rekras Bloodslayer, Kugurum Gorerage, Zasgum Rocksplitter, and Atran Fistmaw. Kargor was faced with a tough decision in the trenches, as his entire force was stranded here. To organize a full retreat would be impossible due to the lack of connection among the trenches. Furthermore, if the Orcs tried to get out of the trenches, Boer snipers could easily pick them off using precision marksmanship. The Bloodsong Offensive could only move upwards, however they had already lost one hundred soldiers and there were three hundred and forty two trenches left to take.

A major problem in the Bloodsong Offensive to begin with was the lack of Goblin engineers or sappers which had been available to those in the other regions of Khaz Modan. This was due to the Goblin engineers largely being called towards the major fronts in Stromgarde and the Siege of Ironforge, both of which were intensive attacks that required more manpower than attacking a small County of Dwarves in the eastern portion of the territory. The majority of Orcish clans in the Arathian Campaign from the Dragonmaws had considered lending aid towards the Eastern front when they had dealt with the conquering of their own soil, however after witnessing the tactical failures of Kargor, they had lost all confidence in leaving soldiers under his command.

Kargor's choice was to continue advancing up the hill towards Goudstad, and attempted to capture as many trenches as he could. In the haze of war, he sent back a message to his courier, who was waiting in the first trench. He would bring word of an extremely fortified stronghold in the east that was very rich with gold and other metals that were required for the war effort, and that if a clan aided in the assault, that they would be rewarded with a portion of this bounty.

The courier's name was a young Orc by the name of Sarfu Laughingsong. Sarfu marched back and carried the message to the ten clans of the Dragonmaw in the Arathi Highlands- the Deadcleavers, the Redtakers, the Redscreams, the Thunderbleeders, the Blackbringers, the Wolfbashers, the Firecrushers, the Wolfeyes, the Tuskhammers, and the Gorescreams. In addition, Sarfu brought the word to four Troll clans in the Hinterlands after hearing from the Orcs about their allies in the southern Hinterlands. The four Troll clans that received word were the Volembi Trolls, the Valajasuwa Trolls, the Kunon'Unjin Trolls, and the Vuzethal Trolls. The four Trolls clans were largely omitted from the ongoing campaign against the Wildhammers, and agreed to join. Of the ten Orcish clans in the Arathi Highlands, only four agreed to support the Bloodsong Offensive. The Wolfbashers and Wolfeyes provided one hundred wolf cavalry, the Thunderbleeders provided five hundred warriors, and the Tuskhammers provided an additional three hundred warriors. The Bloodsong Offensive increased in number nearly overnight, however it would take more than a month's time for the armies to reach the fields of Goudstad. In that time, Kargor had to worry about desertion among his own men, along with starvation. The Orcs had not eaten much since the taking of Goudwater, and the trenches were devoid of most food. The Dwarves had used scorched earth tactics in the trenches, and had dug the food deep into the Earth beforehand. Hunger began to set in among the Orcs around two days into the attack, after they had taken ten trenches. Kargor's attempt on taking another ten trenches failed, and he was only able to take two trenches, and had lost twenty men taking those two trenches alone.

Kargor sent soldiers in the back trenches, which were around fifty men, towards the south, after a messenger had been able to evade the Boer snipers. Fifty Orcs went southwards and attempted to find other sources of food. However, this occurred when Van Ruiter was advancing from the south with his army after defeating the Deadcleavers in Vaalhavn. The fifty man Orc army took up residence in what remained of Goudwater, and were met by the advancing artillerymen of Van Ruiter. It took the Orc army nearly a month to reach Goudwater. Upon reaching Goudwater, they feasted on what scraps remained, but were crushed five days into their occupation when Van Ruiter and his men advanced and decimated the Orcish holders. Van Ruiter and his men also had wagons of food, and set up Goudwater as their staging point against the Orcs of Goudstad. The Orcs were keen on taking Goudstad due to its central route in Zundrboek, as well as its riches. However, messengers of the Count were able to make it across and back up to Krugar's command post in Natalia. Van Ruiter brought word of a victory in the south and that he had reclaimed the settlement of Goudwater, and Krugar wrote back congratulating him and telling him of the situation in Goudstad.

In the thirty five days it had taken the Orcs in Goudwater, Kargor had advanced up nearly thirty trenches. As their hunger increased, as did their bloodlust. Their minds became clouded with anger, and no matter the attacks that were placed on them, they continued despite horrific injuries.

Van Ruiter however, would not be able to supply soldiers when the reinforcements from the other clans arrived. There were nearly nine hundred Orcs advancing northwards in addition to the around two thousand Orcs that remained on the Fields of Goudstad. Van Ruiter knew that his men could not stand a chance against the soldiers, so he advanced northwards after sending word to Krugar. Krugar understood this point, and sent word to the Leader of the Garrison of Goudstad to begin evacuating all the Gold, ammunition, and food to Andriestor. Andriestor and Goudstad had a tunnel between them, which had been dug during the course of the battle. The supplies were beginning to be channeled, and Van Ruiter reached Andriestor nearly thirty days after sending his letter. The Orcish reinforcements arrived in Goudstad when Van Ruiter arrived.

Upon receiving reinforcements, who brought with them food, Kargor's Bloodsong Offensive advanced upwards heavily. The Troll Archers were able to counter the Boer snipers to a certain extent, which meant that the Orcs were not always pinned down. Furthermore, the Wolf cavalry were able to nearly ignore the trenches due to their large size. The additional warriors were able to form a shieldwall to protect them from oncoming attacks by the Boers. When the Orcs had claimed two hundred trenches, there was a full retreat to the city ordered. When the retreat was ordered, the Bloodsong Offensive advanced hastily.

## The Natalia Campaign
The entire city of Goudstad had been emptied over a month, and the soldiers were the last to pass through the tunnel. As they passed through different sections of the tunnel, different parts were destroyed to cover up their tracks. On the sixty fifth day of fighting, the Bloodsong Offensive had reached Goudstad, and found it empty. However, their Orcish allies had brought much food and supplies that the other clans had provided. These clans chose to provide food and supplies but not soldiers. The soldiers had been evacuated to Andriestor, which now had a garrison of around one thousand five hundred soldiers, along with sixty five artillery pieces. Andriestor was the last gamble that Krugar was making, and if Andriestor fell, the war would devolve to guerilla fighting in the outskirts of Natalia. Hundreds of mines were planted in the area surrounding Andriestor, and tunnels were dug connecting it to small farms, which secured food production in the settlement. The preservative of salt allowed for food to be stored for several months in the fort, which totaled up to the fort having over a year's supply of food in case the war dragged on for that long.

Krugar did have another trick up his sleeve in an attempt to stall the Orcish advances. The Orcs were able to get ahold of a map of the County in Goudland, which was inspected by Goblin surveyors. The Goblins determined that a task force could be sent up around Andriestor and strike Natalia. To counter this move, Krugar sent forward the entirety of the Boer Panzer Squadrons. There were four in total, and each was in possession of ten tanks. These ten tanks were powered on steam engines developed in Zundrbar, and were developed in Zundrboek after the Zundrbarians lost contact. The forty tanks were led by Panzercommander Benjamin Hendreksen. Benjamin led forward the panzers towards a ten mile strip of land that was known as the Hendreksen Fortifications. The Hendreksen Fortifications was the area in which the tanks engaged the advancing forces. In addition to having the Four Panzer Divisions, the Freiherr Leonard Longrifles Regiment was sent, with a force of one hundred. The Freiherr Leonard Longrifles Regiment was stationed across four settlements, each settlement having ten supporting panzers. The northernmost settlement, and the one closest to the advancing forces, was Ramsgate. Behind Ramsgate were the three settlements of Ramshead, Ramsforge, and Ramshammer. The four created a region known as the Ram Military Province.

Meanwhile, the Orcish soldiers reached Andriestor after a twenty day march through hard roads and minefields. The gates of Andriestor were forged from reinforced steel, and could only be opened from the inside. There were ten tiers of riflemen who could open fire on the Orcs down at the gates at any time. Additionally, inside the gate, there were numerous Gyrocopter regiments that were sent out for aerial attacks. Gyrocopters were a prototype design of the Engineering Works of Zundrboek Organization, and were hastily militarized and called to arms. The deployment of the Gyrocopters severely affected the outcome of the War, as the Orcs had not brought air superiority into the battle with them. The Arathians lacked little firepower in the air, and thus it was seen of as useless to send in squadrons of Wyvern Riders or Zeppelins.

The Andriestor Garrison was led by Roger van Prinsen, who unfortunately perished after being hit by a Troll archer. After Van Prinsen's death, Van Ruiter was declared the leader of the garrison, and given total command over Andriestor. Krugar Boergraf at this point was becoming extremely nervous, and had already evacuated many of his citizens out onto the naval islands of Svenstad, Janstad, and Andriesstad in the provinces of Kaap and Rijkland. Natalia citizens were being armed to the teeth with whatever they could find, even Krugar himself brought up arms and prepared the citizens of Natalia for war. All of the settlements aside from Andriestor and the Military Province-Ram, were called back to Natalia in case of battle.

The first day of the attack on Andriestor went fairly well for the Bloodsong Offensive. The Bloodsongs smashed through the small military base of Howerd. The Bloodsong Offensive murdered all the remaining defenders of Howerd, however it was renowned for having a garrison of fifty and still standing up against the threat of the Bloodsong Offensive.

The Battle of Andriestor however soon turned sour after the Orcs were forced to get dug in as they could not breach the fort. They attempted to keep the fort pinned down for as much as possible, however this required many arrows. Much of the munitions had gone unused in the Battle of Goudstad, and this set of munitions had been sent back to Andriestor.

Van Ruiter held the fort though, and brooded about what he could do next. There was no real tactical disadvantage of holding Andriestor, and the fate of the County lay in the Military Province of Ram more so than in the Siege of Andriestor. The Bloodsong Offensive's numbers began to drop, as they started to once more run out of food. This occurred on the fifteenth day of the siege. The Orcs began to be taken by bloodlust, and in a fit of anger, Kargor is known to have slaughtered two trolls and fed them to his men for questioning orders and supplying the suggestion of a possible retreat.

Van Ruiter knew that the Orcish lines were steadily falling apart based off of what had happened in Goudstad. The soldiers had only brought so much food, and the Orcs began to turn on one another. Within no time, the Troll archers left the army after they were disrespected constantly. Kargor started to go insane and bludgeoned his son for calling out against his tactical decisions. In another fit of rage, he ordered a full scale attack on Andriestor. Andriestor opened its gates, but the opening of the gates held a new surprise for the Orcs- flamethrowers. Flamethrowers had been in use in Zundrboek for some time, and came in use now. Once the Orcs had entered, the Boers sprung out and unleashed a blaze of hell onto them, along with hundreds of rifle bullets. In the madness, Kargor was known to have been slain by Van Ruiter, who sliced his head off using a bayonet as his corpse burned. To this day, Kargor's head is displayed in the Royal Vault of the Boergraf Family. However, Van Ruiter was killed by an arrow from a Troll. He did not die instantly, however the wound caused an infection to form which killed him over a period of two weeks. Krugar Boergraf was known to have travelled to Andriestor and spoken personally with Van Ruiter on his deathbed. Van Ruiter's last words were known to have been, "The County lives on in you- Krugar, may the Fatherland live on."

Meanwhile, in the Military Province of Ram, things had entered a stalemate in Ramsgate from the beginning. Ramsgate's soldiers kept the advancing army pinned down, and the advancing army kept the Ramsgate Soldiers pinned down. After hearing word of a victory in Andriestor, the four other groups met up with the Ramsgate defenders and charged forward, defeating the remaining Orcs and Goblins in the city. Together, the Orcs were stamped out and the Boar War ended officially after nearly three months of fighting, when a final group of twenty soldiers was found trying to escape the highlands on the Vaal River. Van Ruiter's son- Dominic Van Ruiter, was known to have used the same cannons used in the Battle of Vaalstad to destroy the Orcish boats.

## Memory and Legacy
To this day, the War of the Boar is known to be a defining part of the leadership skills of Krugar Boergraf. A museum was dedicated several weeks after the end of the war for all wartime artifacts to be collected inside of.

Under the reign of Rundon Boergraf, a memorial was created in the capital city of Kaapstad to the loyal defenders, and engraved were the names of all those who had died in the war.

The defeat in the War of the Boar is known to have been a major source of hatred for the Dragonmaw Orcs against the Boers and the Dwarves of Zundrbar in general, as the Dragonmaw Clans also lost to the Dwarves of Zundrbar in the Angerfang Wars, which preceded the War of the Boar by around a month.
